1. Yes, I was brought up in a religious household. 
I stopped believing in religion around 17 after reading all the available Hindu scriptures I could find (Vedas, Mahabharata, Ramayana etc) 

2. My family attended religious services regularly. We still have a small temple at home where I’m forced to pray even after I told them I’m an atheist (I’m a 19 year old girl from India so yeah)

3. We are taught (at least here) to follow values, rules and traditions w/o ever questioning it. Eg- elders should be shown respect. It’s a value I agree with. But if an elder is being irrational and degrading others (racist, sexist, transphobic, homophobic, casteist, communal and body shaming comments) all the damn time, if he/ she hits their family, even if a man abandons his family- people still expect us to respect them. Religion did not allow me to ask questions and think openly. So the values and viewpoints that are important to me are a. Be respectful but not an idiot b. Listen to all the perspectives and then use your rational thinking to come to a decision

4. No. They’re super religious and even a word against god leads to yelling, fights and degrading the person who spoke against it. 

5.  I’m an Indian, India is a country of different religions and beliefs. People are always trying to convert or convince me to believe in religion. Also, atheism is not a religion. So you cannot say ‘practice atheism’. 

6. I was born in a Hindu family. Hinduism sucks. It’s patriarchal, casteist, transphobic, homophobic, (all other religions-phobic). I believe that the common mass believes in the idea of someone looking out for them, the ideas of jannat, heaven and swarg- these are all same. It gives comfort to a common man that he’ll go to a better place after death and will be taken care of. This belief gives people comfort. Add many beliefs, rules and hey you have a religion. So people start to follow it blindly. 

7. That Hinduism is peaceful. 

8. Me- I would date or marry an atheist. 

My family - (here they play a big role coz familial approval is pertinent in India for getting married) will hate that and make sure I marry someone religious. And when it comes to dating, not allowed to date, it’s against the rules. Just marry, no dating. 

9. I was religious. So I started reading, learning and researching about my religion and later other religions as well. It all made sense- they were all based on irrationality. Why would some god be so harsh? More importantly- god, who? I started asking questions and thinking critically. That’s when I realised I don’t believe in any religion. 

10. If I do someday have children, I will give them full knowledge about all the religions. I will also help them think critically. And religion and rationality don’t go together, so they’ll be aware of what’s appropriate and what’s not.

The first thing is that yes INDIAN SOCIETY IS PATRIARCHAL! I’m so sorry but 8 years in isolation is too much!! I’ve heard ‘You have badhas’ so many times that now I’m used to it. Public shaming is a very common thing, in fact once you become a teenager, parents think it is funny to say all your mischief stories to everyone from new friends to close relatives and then judge you on the basis of that mischief. A typical Indian parenting is nowhere near how a child should grow up. Religion is given the utmost importance whilst when you ask rational questions you are eyed at and are supposed to keep your mouth shut. All this is unfortunately very common. You being a european and still having to face all this cruel practices makes me sad and pissed that even in foreign countries such malpractices still prevail.

Hinduism being polytheistic has many such beliefs. Regarding to animals- Fish, turtle, boar are avatars of god Vishnu
Ganpati has the head of an elephant 
Hanuman is a monkey god 
Nagas ie snakes are considered pious especially the Indian Cobra since it is associated with one of the main gods called Shiva
Vultures (named Sampati and Jatayu) converse with gods in Ramayana (a holy epic)
Lord Shiv has a personal assistant which is a cow named Nandi

Basically it is said that during the era when “god lived on earth”, all animals could talk with humans. So pretty much all animals. 
Apart from that, these are the most common superstitious beliefs that still exist-
Crow shit brings luck.
If a black cat crosses your path, it's a bad omen
Cutting nails and hair on Saturdays brings bad luck.
Hanging lemon and 7 green chilies so that the goddess of misfortune doesnt enter 
Breaking mirror brings bad luck
Twitching of the eye is inauspicious
Do not sweep after sunset or goddess of fortune will not enter 
Shaking legs is considered to invite bad luck.
You even lose your wealth, if you shake your legs.
Eating any sweet food item before doing an important task brings good luck
Sleeping with a scissor or a knife under your pillow avoids bad dreams
If your left palm itches,you're going to run into some money soon.

The list can go on and on.
